_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.lead: The first Doodle was an out of office note
beats.text: In August 1998 Larry Page and Sergey Brin published the first Doodle to say they were away at Burning Man.
beats.note: Google's Doodles page dates it to 30 August 1998.

beats.name: Dennis Hwang
beats.role: Asked by Page and Brin to design a Bastille Day logo in 2000, his first Doodle.

beats.lead: Then the logo started to move
beats.text: The first animated Doodle ran on 31 October 2000, for Halloween.
beats.note: The first interactive one came ten years later.

beats.lead: And then you could play it
beats.text: On 21 May 2010 a playable Pac-Man logo marked the game's 30th anniversary.
beats.note: Google calls it the first interactive Doodle game experience.

beats.context: Google says it has made more than this over the decades.

beats.line: It began as a note on the door.
